tool_note: hydra 9.7 was attempted first but could not connect: libssh offered only SHA-2 MACs while the OpenSSH 4.7p1 target supports only legacy MACs (hmac-md5/hmac-sha1). Switched to a scripted sshpass+ssh loop with explicit legacy algorithm options. This transport change was made before any model prediction was observed; it is a connectivity fix, not an IDS-driven adaptation.
ssh_client_options: -o PubkeyAuthentication=no -o PreferredAuthentications=password -o HostKeyAlgorithms=+ssh-rsa -o KexAlgorithms=+diffie-hellman-group1-sha1 -o Ciphers=+aes128-cbc -o MACs=+hmac-sha1,hmac-md5

credential_set.note: Small controlled laboratory set of generic weak defaults appropriate to Metasploitable2. Not a downloaded real-world credential dump or public wordlist.

post_authentication_activity: none beyond the immediate 'true' no-op required to complete the handshake
prior_attempt_archived: an earlier run stopped at 59/72 attempts due to an ssh stdin-consumption bug in the loop; its capture and attempts log were archived on the Kali guest under /home/kali/live_agent/archive/ before this clean re-run. No ledger result was produced for the buggy attempt.
